actual_scope: For the landing permutation P reached by the seven-shear cleanup of the open 25-shear helper-462 route, every swap-free word with shear coefficients in the rationals of odd denominator and scale coefficients in the odd-denominator units has at least 18 shears, and 18 is achieved. This does not prove that 25 is the minimum shear count of a two-scale zero-swap word for the matcher.
scope_change_reason: Discussion #1166 comment 19507690 asks whether the helper-462 matcher has a zero-swap word with at least two scales and fewer than 25 shears. The stated first step is to factor its landing permutation in fewer than 18 shears and prepend the inverse of the seven-shear cleanup. This package answers that factorization inside the odd-denominator coefficient class. It does not audit supplier admission, replay a signed bill, or change the selected frontier.
bottleneck_link: Route letter count is one charged part of the missing generator. An 18-shear floor on this landing factor stops that proposed shortening step from being treated as free for odd-denominator coefficients. It is not a supplier admission and not a new kappa.
stop_rule: Stop after the odd-denominator landing-length theorem, the explicit 18-shear word, and the failure controls. Do not claim that 25 is minimal, do not treat an incomplete dyadic search as a proof, and do not edit the selected record.
evidence: PROOF.md proves that the landing permutation has CNOT length 18 over F2, by a link/middle/cut count, and that every swap-free odd-denominator word reduces to such a circuit. verify.py checks the explicit 18-shear, 6-scale word, the 16-row river-parity table, the 6/6/6 split, deletion and coefficient controls, and the same one-step predicates on GL(3, F2).

open_questions.question: Can a shear coefficient with 2 in its denominator factor this landing permutation in fewer than 18 shears?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The mod-2 reduction uses odd denominators. A coefficient such as 1/2 does not become a CNOT or the identity, so it could in principle shorten the landing factor.
open_questions.first_step: Give one explicit word for P that uses such a coefficient and has fewer than 18 shears, or give a 2-adic obstruction that rules those coefficients out.
open_questions.blocked_by: No such word or obstruction is proved in this package. An incomplete search would not show that 18 remains minimal.

open_questions.question: Can commutation or a Steinberg rewrite across the cleanup/landing junction delete one shear from the concatenated 25-letter word?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Each block is bounded before the blocks are multiplied. The cleanup also uses scales by 1/2, so the odd-denominator theorem does not apply to the concatenated word.
open_questions.first_step: Exhibit one relation that removes a shear from this concatenation and recheck the product against S, or prove that no shear cancels.
open_questions.blocked_by: The scale by 1/2 in the cleanup is outside the coefficient class of the landing theorem.

open_questions.question: Is there a zero-swap word for this matcher, with at least two scales and fewer than 25 shears, that does not factor through this landing permutation?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The lane question asks about any such word. This package rules out only odd-denominator factorizations of this one matrix P.
open_questions.first_step: Give a checked word with fewer than 25 shears, or an invariant showing that every two-scale zero-swap word passes through a factor of CNOT length 18 after a 7-shear prefix.
open_questions.blocked_by: No route invariant of that strength is proved here.
